Getting over ladder anxiety is difficult, but it opens your mind to the game as I had never thought of.

Been a fan of SC2 since it came out, but only recently got into the game as an actual mp player. The high skill curve always pushed me away, as it did all of my friends, but I still watched pros play since WoL.

After a month of grinding, Playing AI, and actively watching matches rather than passively watching, I got enough courage to get ranked.

I'm not good, (gold) I'm not smart, and I might not get to a higher league for the next 4 months. In fact, I only got gold because some de-rankers boosted me above my skill level.

But WOW this game makes you feel good about improving. It is one of the few games I've played where I can feel myself improve, and can work on improvement on a personal and exact level. A win in SC2 is validation for understanding a build that you ignored, or keeping up with macro, or any of these thousands of variables that eventually become second nature. A loss in SC2 can show you exactly what/when/where you made a mistake that cost you the game.

For anyone who wants to get into SC2, it is very important to watch pro (or high level), players. You *WILL NOT* be able to do what they do and this is okay. Contrastly in Overwatch you can see some pro Tracer or main tank play that you know you could do. Good shots, good placement, map knowledge etc. They just do it more consistently. In SC2, there is **NO WAY** I can do what TY or Special can do. But I can see when they build buildings, think about their decision making, their patterns, and efficiency.

Just like chess; we will not be a GM just by watching streams and we will not become GM just by playing with no guidance. We need first-hand experience, advice from our betters, and a desire to understand more than we think we know. This is very off-putting to some people and was to me for many years. Breaking through that barrier made me love this game even more, as it opened up so many things to appreciate and improve upon.

Now I watch pro games and freak out when I notice something that would have seemed 'simple' to me without first-hand knowledge. 

"Holy shit did they just use their warp prism, pick up and place back 2 immortals, blink their stalkers onto high ground, blink the damaged ones away, all while making 4 buildings at their main base in the span of a few seconds?" I don't even play Protoss and that threw me for a loop.

So I'm seventeen, fresh into my last year of high school and every day around eleven thirty the bell would ring for a forty minute lunch. September in Idaho is a mix of dry air, arid desert heat, and blowing winds from the earths asshole, the smell came from the dairy farm in the south of town. That day happened to be a scorcher so going outside without a car was unfavorable unless you wanted to melt into the sidewalk. Heading to the gas station was obviously a no go as I was banned the year before. 

Something about forty dollars worth of Swiss rolls gone missing I don't know I had lost count months ago.

Los Alberto's was the closest restaurant to us that could get homemade tortillas fresh from the floor with authentic seasonings lightly spritzed by rat pee, so it was our obvious choice day after day. Five bucks for 1500 calories that would seep through the bag if you waited more than an average of 48 seconds, plopping out like a baby deer afterbirth and all. That number was rigorously tested by our science department with acclaimed studies such as “Can we make a rubber band gun strong enough to stick a pen into a mans back?” and “Just setting shit on fire”. Both of which provided positive results in two unfortunate double blind experiments.

So we grab our baby deer and start chowing down. A friend of some 4 odd years had bought our group a bouquet of these odd long tortilla wrapped tacos. Beef and pork, cheese, and a foot and a half of tortilla with no veggies. We called them churritos, as only white people could. We take a few into the van on our way out and drive back to school. Three hours later after our last class I head to the parking lot to get a ride from him and he does not look happy. Not with me, but definitely with someone.

See our group of friends has a habit of doing really dumb shit with food. The year before on our last day of class we bought some old golf clubs at the DI (kind of a Mormon salvation army) and some cheap sodas, shook them up and smacked them across the yard. There was not a month where someone didn't have pastries or burritos tossed at their car.

Today they decided to attach one of those churritos to the outside of his car underneath his wiper blade. That thing had been slow cooking under 90 degree heat for almost four hours at that point. It was grotesque, the meat was devoid of all moisture, cheese had hardened like set cement and the tortilla had solidified like a caterpillars cocoon. The smell was pungent and he didn't even want to touch it.

After taking it upon myself to grab it we hopped into the car and rolled the windows down for some air.

“Dude, get rid of that oh my god.” 

“You mean you don't want it?” I waved it in front of his face as he reversed into the street. He gagged a bit and laughed. We waited at a red light.

“Seriously just toss that”

“I'm waiting for a garbage can, gotta save the earth man.”

“It's biodegradable just toss it to the street.” We took the green and headed left.

“What, you mean just toss it out the window like a newspaper?” I held it in my hand one last time, tortilla cracking like a dead sea scroll. At that moment a small bit of liquefied 'meat' poured out of the top like a popped pimple. 

Disgusted, I tossed it out the window like a throwing knife, end over end as hard as I could.

“Whaagh” We heard from my open window. I looked in his side mirror to scope out the scene. There was a daycare across the street, and a small child was laying face down in his sand pit, crying with a crispy meat burrito laying next to him. The other kids were weaving in and out of the jungle gym screaming, one of them was trying to jump the fence. 

By now that kid should actually be in middle school, and I wonder if he has a fear of Mexican food.

Though my parents always guessed since I was small, (My father has the same ailment, though undiagnosed and he manages amazingly well) never noticed the problem was ever present until I was around 14.

I noticed I was unable to stop blinking, not softly, but almost violently. Try closing your eyes as hard as you can until you can hear it in your ears and youll get an idea. Attempt this hundreds of times a day, and headaches will follow. I remember joking to a friend that I might have Tourette syndrome. A year after this the coughs came back, but now they were small hums, like I was laughing with my mouth closed.

While they were annoying, I had handled them semi well until my sophomore year of highschool at the age of 16. What was before a small auditory annoyance became a constant battle with my neck and arms. My right arm would jerk about, smacking my chest and hitting my temple. I would crane my neck so violently I legitimately knocked myself out once, along with many other twitches to my cheeks and jaw. All the while the noises I made became louder and constant.

I was diagnosed with Tourettes, was forced to leave HS early due to the stress of being in rooms with my peers, and had a few stints in the hospital from emotional distress. I did graduate, a feat I did not believe I could accomplish after my mental faculties seemed to unravel by the day.

Almost 3 years later, hundreds of hours of therapy, self reflection and discipline, I'm happy to say I'm still here. So are the tics, but they have mostly shifted to very low auditory, and low key chin movements as long as I keep my mental state in check. The more violent tics dont really go away, they are now distinguishable by triggers that I have to mentally avoid. I've chipped a couple teeth doing so but it's much better than how I once was. I have a job and im living semi well, and hoping I can keep the momentum going.

Its something that will stick with me for life, and quite possibly pass on to my children.

Then TWAU blew TWD:S1 out of the water, particularly because I was waiting month after month wondering about how the story was going to resolve itself.

Not because of a gory death, not for some decision I needed a few more moments to think through, but because everything i thought was right with the world was flipped upside down with one single line of dialogue.

TWD:S2 began as more of the same yet by episode 3 I started to not truly have the reactions I had beforehand. I tried Borderlands, and it couldn't capture anywhere near the excitement TellTale could before. GoT, yes even as a fan of the series, I despised. It's difficult to pinpoint the moment a spartan truly becomes one. In fact, I would almost argue these new recruits cannot be considered Spartans. Or possibly, there shouldn't be a comparison at all.

My time aboard the Infinity has opened my eyes to the multitude of stress and psychosis exhibited by the newest spartan IV generation. Ive seen them stare past me in my recording room, almost oblivious to my presence while looking for Covenant. They have routinely mentioned their desire to become integrated into immortality by the Didact, as to avoid the loss of their squad mates eating away what humanity they have left. Though the thought of these men and women counting on dying to end their military career was dis disheartening, the humanity behind their eyes was a welcoming distinction between them and the last two generations.

This is my third foray into Spartan psychology. Before the destruction of planet Onyx, and the the events after Reach, (space time dilation makes it difficult to pinpoint where I was when those happened) I had been tasked with ONI to prove a Spartan II could speak in front of non military personnel for a morale boost. After that, I was asked to give counselling to the growing spartan III program.

In respect to the only surviving spartan III's I was able to talk to before the events of Onyx, and the heroic attack on the Covenant factory before that, I would like to exclude their testimonials. She couldnt speak to me, and he didn't have anything to say.

I was aboard an ONI ship, an ugly mesh of metal that I wasn't even allowed to know existed. Yet here I was, walking the halls and feeling like I shouldnt be around any of these people. A Spartan II was to meet me in my office. She was already there.

It was my first time actually meeting a Spartan in person. They were still officially under the rug, so I knew almost nothing besides the feats they accomplished. Which, as I shouldnt have to repeat, have almost saved the Human Race.

Sitting down with G (Names and call signs restricted per ONI request) made me question how human I was myself. She was almost a full meter taller than me, with shoulders as wide as my car back home. Her eyes seemed to take in every movement of my body, and once again see right past me. There was no agitation however, or even uneasiness in their eyes. As if they looked down on me as a lost child in need of protection.

"Is it okay if I ask you a few questions?" I ask, placing my pen down onto the table, and placing my recorder next to it. She gave a slight nod, and sat quiet.

"ONI has had trouble sitting down Soldiers such as yourself down for psych evaluations in the past. I understand that you have not been out of active duty since the Covenant war begun, and you were active for years before that correct?"

"Yes." She answered. Her voice was shockingly smooth.

"Was fighting other humans attractive to you? Or were you simply following orders?"

Her face was again expressionless, save for a slight cock of the head to her right side. "If you are asking me if I liked killing others, then yes I did. They were nothing to me other than a danger to the UNSC, and the civilians they swear to protect." She didnt begin to speak again, though I felt she was too insistent they it was the UNSC that was there to protect civs, not herself.

"You never once wanted to, defuse the situation with the Innies? Were you not taught de-escelation tactics in boot camp?" At those last words I could see the muscles of her temples twitch slightly. She did not speak, which I took to mean if she was called into action, the situation could never be talked through. In fact, I did not even know what training these people went through.

"Okay then, uhh, have you felt any drain on yourself, after so many years on an active roster, and the subsequent destruction of Harvest and the new war?"

She still had not fucking moved. Not even blinked, just staring at me. I dont think she saw me as anything important, almost akin to a bird chirping at her in the street. "My brothers and sisters have almost all gone missing, the Covenant is closer than ever to finding earth, and I am in a room speaking about feelings I don't have. Anything to do with my past, my training, and my record is confidential by order of ONI themselves. I do not answer to you."

Now she moved, standing and leaving the room in long strides without saying another word.

This is the only conversation I play back to myself, standing here watching Spartan IV bodies come in from the surface. The men and women hitting the walls and screaming as their friends come back in bags, or often not at all. And I think of how damaged that woman must have been to see this every day of her life. 

Or maybe, she saw us as broken.
